evidence.detail: .menu has flex:1 and position:relative but no overflow-y, so the menu column cannot scroll independently of the nav
.submenu already has overflow-y: auto, but cannot scroll independently for the same structural reason
.submenu is position:absolute; top:0, positioned relative to .menu — if .menu scrolls, the submenu's top:0 is off-screen when the menu is scrolled down
nav { overflow-y: auto } causes the whole nav column to scroll as a single unit instead of menu/submenu scrolling independently

triage.fix_sketch: In shared_web/static/css/pd.css: (1) Add overflow-y: auto to .menu (around line 804). (2) Change .submenu from position:absolute;top:0 to position:fixed;top:0;left:var(--main-menu-width) so it anchors to the viewport rather than .menu's scroll origin, or move position:relative from .menu to nav so the submenu is positioned relative to the full nav height. All changes are in pd.css only, ~5-15 lines.
triage.notes: Choosing position:fixed for .submenu would need to be excluded from the medium-width media query where the submenu is already a popover; careful testing of all three responsive breakpoints (narrow/medium/wide) is needed.
